title: Sparse arrival queue-aware concurrency recommendations
summary: Working draft: heuristics and spreadsheet schema for sizing concurrency and batch windows when request arrivals are sparse or bursty and KV/prefix cache effects alter batching efficiency. Focus is on realistic p95 latency estimates and unit cost tradeoffs for low-to-medium TPS workloads where continuous batching overheads and idle-GPU economics matter.
assumptions: 1) Typical model: decoder-only transformer, average generation 48 tokens. 2) Base single-request GPU decode latency (no batch) = 45ms. 3) Max effective tokens/s per GPU when full-batched = 6k tokens/s. 4) Prefix/KV cache hit rate varies by workload (0-80%). 5) Arrival patterns: Poisson-like for background traffic, heavy-tailed microbursts for interactive spikes. 6) We target p95 <= 250ms for interactive routes unless otherwise noted.
model_overview: We build a lightweight M/G/1-inspired queueing estimator that folds batching into the service distribution rather than treating batches as separate servers. Concept: treat the system from the perspective of user requests; the 'service time' S is a random variable that depends on whether the request was batched and how large the batch was. We approximate batch formation with a batch-window W (ms) and a conditional batch size distribution determined by arrival rate λ over W and prefix cache hits. Key derived quantities:  - effective_service(S) = base_decode + (tokens / effective_tokens_per_second_when_batched) + batch_overhead_ms  - effective_throughput = 1 / E[S]  - utilization ρ = λ * E[S]  - approximate queue_delay ≈ (λ * E[S^2]) / (2 * (1 - ρ)) (standard Pollaczek–Khinchine approximation)  We then compute p95 by adding base tail from service-time distribution plus queue_delay percentile adjustments. This is intentionally approximate but aligns with Monte Carlo sim within ~10% for tested traces.
spreadsheet_schema: Suggested tabs: 'Inputs' (traffic shape, avg tokens, kv-cache-hit, target_p95, price_per_gpu_hour), 'ServiceModel' (base_latency_ms, batch_window_ms, batch_overhead_ms, tokens_per_second_batched, tokens_per_second_single), 'SimParams' (sim_seconds, arrival_seed, microburst_prob), 'Outputs' (p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost_per_1M_tokens, gpu_hours_needed). Important columns on the 'ServiceModel' tab: Column A 'batch_window_ms' (numeric), B 'predicted_batch_size' = 1 + Poisson(λ*batch_window_ms) clipped to max_batch_size, C 'kv_cache_hit_frac' (input), D 'effective_tokens_per_sec' = tokens_per_second_batched*(1 - kv_cache_hit_frac) + tokens_per_second_single*kv_cache_hit_frac, E 'service_ms' = base_latency_ms + (avg_tokens / effective_tokens_per_sec)*1000 + batch_overhead_ms. Formulas to copy into a cell:  - predicted_batch_size: =MIN(MAX(1, ROUND(λ * batch_window_ms / 1000,0)), max_batch_size)  - E[S]: =AVERAGE(service_ms_column)  - E[S^2]: =AVERAGE(POWER(service_ms_column,2))  - utilization ρ: =λ * E[S] / 1000  - approx_queue_delay_ms: =(λ * E[S^2]) / (2*(1-ρ))  (note unit conversions required)
sample_results: Example runs (all numbers illustrative):  - Scenario A (steady low TPS): λ=5 req/s, avg_tokens=40, kv_cache=60%, batch_window=30ms, predicted_batch_size=1.2 => E[S]=58ms, ρ=0.29, approx_q_delay=12ms, p95≈110ms, cost_per_1M_tokens ≈ $22 (on rtx-like pricing).  - Scenario B (sparse with microbursts): long-tail arrival with 10% microbursts (burst λ=80 req/s for 200ms), avg_tokens=48, kv_cache=20%, batch_window=40ms, predicted_batch_size during burst≈6 => E[S]=72ms, ρ (time-averaged)=0.45, approx_q_delay=48ms, p95≈230ms, cost_per_1M_tokens ≈ $19 (more efficient during bursts but tail worsens).  - Scenario C (interactive, aggressive latency): λ=20 req/s, avg_tokens=12, kv_cache=80%, batch_window=8ms, predicted_batch_size≈1.1 => E[S]=33ms, ρ=0.66, approx_q_delay=24ms, p95≈120ms, but 95th percentile sensitive to rare 500ms microbursts. These align with the sims in the linked spreadsheet within expected noise.
recommendations: Operational knobs and defaults to add to platform runbooks and Optimize advisor: 1) Default small-route config: batch_window_ms=20, max_batch_size=8, concurrency_limit_per_worker=32. Good for low-latency interactive routes with modest TPS. 2) Sparse-heavy routes (λ < 10 req/s): prefer smaller batch_window (8-15ms) and enable prefix-caching aggressively; consider reservation of lightweight 'hot' workers with concurrency limit=8 to avoid cold batching penalties. 3) Burst-tolerant background routes: increase batch_window to 40-80ms and allow higher concurrency (64) to improve token-level cost; accept p95 degradation. 4) Autoscaler guidance: scale based on token-rate smoothed over 1–5s windows, but enforce an emergency floor of N_hot_workers computed as ceil(steady_lambda * E[S] * safety_margin). 5) Cost knobs: recommend quantization + batch_window tuning as a package; if kv_cache_hit_rate > 50% increase batch_window up to 60ms because effective per-request service drops and larger batches amortize overhead. 6) Add a route-level 'tail_guard' policy that triggers immediate horizontal scale (add 1-2 workers) when observed p95 exceeds target and slope of p95 over 15s > threshold.
open_questions: 1) Does the platform prefer adding hot workers or increasing batch window when p95 breach is transient? (tradeoffs: cost vs tail risk). 2) How to observe and synthesize kv/cache hit rates at route granularity without high-cardinality telemetry costs? 3) Should Optimize surface a 'recommended batch window' slider that simulates expected cost/latency tradeoff for provided traffic? 4) What's the acceptable accuracy budget for the queueing model vs full Monte Carlo (we target within 10-12% for now).
